label: lem:genus-from-hecke-completeness
title: Genus from Hecke completeness for torus knots
html:
Lemma. Genus from Hecke completeness for torus knots

Let N(g) be the number of torus knots T_{r,s} with r \in \{2, 3\} whose Seifert genus (r-1)(s-1)/2 is at most g. Then g = 4 is the least genus at which N(g) \geq 5, the number of irreducibles of H_2(q) \oplus H_3(q).

This is a statement about the count of available evaluations, and it is all that is proved here. It does not say that the evaluations available at g = 4 span the 5-dimensional representation: N(4) = 6 vectors in a 5-dimensional space need not span it, and here they provably do not. The spanning statement is separated out as the block-rank remark, which records that the evaluation matrix has rank 4 at g = 4, not 5.
